messages:
maya: Heads-up — got flagged by sales: CompetitorX launched a tier today with embeddings at 50% price and advertised 2x throughput. Customer asks already in: 'can we match price/latency for embeddings?'. Need quick call on scope.

leah: +1, multiple AE threads. Major pilot customer asked for a cost-comparison doc. They're pushing renewal in 6w.

diego: can you paste the link or deck? curious on their constraints (quantization, batch limits, sequence length).

leah: https://example.com/competitorx-announce — they call it "Embeddings Lite". Note: only supports 1024-d and fixed batching 128.

sam: if it's fixed batching that's a huge caveat. Our Serving runtime can do adaptive batching + KV cache; we can probably keep latency advantage on tiny queries.

riley: also check if they're using a lower-dim model or PQ/IVF at the index level. Cheaper doesn't always mean same quality.

maya: high-level ask from sales: 1) short-term playbook to respond to RFPs/procurement 2) product decision: do we prioritize a parity-priced embedding tier or lean into quality/perf differentiation?

diego: short-term we can: a) produce a cost/quality comparison sheet b) add a documented guidance page: "when to pick Redwood embeddings vs Embeddings Lite" c) adjust routing policy to prefer our lower-latency model for small seqs. Low lift.

sam: medium-term: we could add a fixed-price embed SKU with lower memory footprint by shipping a quantized 8-bit variant. Engineering effort: ~3 sprint spike + 2 sprints to stabilize. Risk: could increase maintenance matrix.

riley: we should define clear evals (M-Recall@10, MRR, bias tests) and customer-facing quality baselines before any price-focused SKU. If we drop quality thresholds we lose trust.

leah: Sales needs an answer in 10 business days for renewal talks. If it takes 2 months to build, they'll lose the deal. Can we offer a commercial discount right now tied to SLA/commitment?

maya: Options on the table: 1) Go-to-market discount program (sales-owned) + comms + comparison doc (fast) 2) Product parity SKU (quantized embedding) — higher engineering cost 3) Double-down on differentiation (latency, observability, hmm) and sell value. Need to pick what we commit to.

diego: recommend staged approach: A) immediate comms + discount → buys time. B) run experiment to evaluate quantized variant (spike sprints) with clear success criteria. C) If spike shows <5% quality degradation and 30% cost reduction, greenlight parity SKU.

sam: technical success criteria to measure in spike: 1) inference latency P95 <= current P95 + 5ms for <=128 tokens 2) embedding cosine correlation >= 0.985 vs baseline on embed-eval set 3) memory footprint reduction >= 30% 4) CPU/GPU ops don't increase inference tail significantly.

riley: add business success criteria: 1) Sales sign-off that price delta closes deals in pilot accounts 2) No regression alerts during 72h canary 3) Monitoring hooks for quality drift (per-customer evals).

maya: agree. who owns the spike? diego owns eng coordination; riley owns evals; leah drives pilot accounts and discount comms; sam helps with implementation. I'll write PRD-lite after this thread.

leah: for sales comms I need a one-pager + competitor FAQ. Can we get that by EOD tomorrow?

sam: I can mock the technical FAQ tonight (short bullets). diego can confirm feasibility bits.

diego: will sync with infra on capacity impact. If we expose quantized SKU we need an autoscale knob to avoid noisy-neighbor issues in Dedicated. That might be additional infra work but not blocking the spike.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: spike-repo branch 'quant-spike' created by sam at 1762504399.

maya: timeline proposal: Day 0 (today): comms + discount playbook. Day 3: prd-lite and spike kickoff. Day 10: spike results + go/no-go. Day 30: if greenlight, pilot SKU with 1-2 customers and 72h canary.

leah: that timeline aligns with sales needs. If we push the discount, please give me exact language (T&Cs).

riley: I'll prepare eval datasets (semantic-ops, retrieval-bench, internal priority set). Need access to pilot customer data for realistic checks — leah can coordinate.

sam: quick note — if we expose cheaper SKU we must surface it clearly in Console with a "quality tier" label and explicit migration guidance (embedding dims, downstream retraining notes). We shouldn't surprise customers.

diego: agreed. also add rollback and automatic fallback to full-precision model if quality telemetry crosses threshold. That keeps risk low.

maya: final decision for this thread: proceed with staged approach. I'll draft PRD-lite and owner list. If anyone has blockers speak up now.

leah: none from sales; I need the one-pager by EOD.

riley: no blockers.

sam: none. I'll push the spike branch and share the runbook.

diego: I'll schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow 10am to finalize acceptance criteria.

maya: thanks team — will post the PRD link here when ready. :thumbsup:
